questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city history, as well as the motivation for learning to speak German.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. Communication with host University as well as Erasmus was very slow and often not very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Very little. Had to find much needed information myself, often done through other students, since information on curriculums as well as practical aspects were in many cases neither elaborate nor helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Personally, I used social media, where I had a very fluent and easy experience finding good and affordable housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Recommendable, if you like to live more independant.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am aware, that I got lucky with my own housing, and that the appartement/WG-market can be tricky in Berlin. In my own experience, I was 5 satisfied, but had I not had luck, it would have been a lower grade.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very unintuitive system, especially for Erasmus students used to other types.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process seemed to me outdated, anarchistic and unnecessarily time consuming and stress provoking. People applied for more courses than they intended to attend, which led to chaotic classes in which teachers had no idea, how many students attended class. It seemed like no one, not even the administration had a clear idea of the course organisation, and I personally had very many problems finding out how to organise my classes.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not very much help was available - often there passed weeks before my mails were answered, and it seemed like the administrative staff expected Erasmus students to be comfortable with a very manual, non-digital course registration process in German, which for me not was very simple.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very succesfull. When I finally had chosen courses, that were offered after I left, OLA took 6 weeks to recognise my courses, and decide, that I had chosen wrong ones. This was a very stressfull experience, to find out, that I attended wrong courses in the middle of the semester/June.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Rather choose not so attractive courses, than being in need of ECTS points to succeed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Some courses seemed at extremely high level, where others, combined BA and MA courses were more basic and focused on rote learning.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The UCPH style is in general more critical and academic, which I like better, where the HU style is more focused on building knowledge by heart without being too critical towards sources.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: A combination of academic courses and internship, which had good learning outcome.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "Musikpraxis" was a really lovely experience. I also did a German Course which was great!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very good opportunities for social hobby life!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I played in an orchestra, which was a fantastic experience.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Musik an der HU!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the opera - the Abendkasse youth tickets cost only 15 euro one hour before performance, where you receive best available seats and it is world class, esp. Staatsoper unter den Linden!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy, since I was so keen in learning about the culture and language. The German "Ordnung muss sein"-mentality can be really annoying though.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Learn German!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
"Ordnung muss sein", especially with corona
restrictions.Very
strange to live a place where everyone wear Darth Vader looking masks and think it makes corona go away, but people still shake hands all the time while very few cares about washing their hands regularly and keeping distance which has not been a very visible part of the strategy here. I feel much more exposed to Covid through this strategy than I do in Denmark even though I don't care about the illness very much.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The cultural heritage: Architecture, literature, music, theater, history!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Have patience with courses. Go experience the rich culture. Learn German!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning German, experiencing culture. Everything non-academic.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The general administration at the HU as well as mobility online huge stacks of documentation requirements, which was badly coordinated with my own university as well as OLA - very slow communication. In germany: , "Ordnung muss sein" and the very exhausting Maskenpflicht, where citizens non-critical approach and lack of logic in wearing this without doing anything else made it strenuous to be present at many public places.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
